bind_address.description: IP address the daemon binds to (e.g., '127.0.0.1' for localhost only, or '0.0.0.0' for all interfaces).

bind_port.description: TCP port for incoming connections (must be ≥1024 unless running as root).

private_key_path.description: Absolute path to the server’s private key file (PEM format).

certificate_path.description: Absolute path to the server’s public certificate file (PEM format).

max_connections.description: Maximum number of concurrent client connections allowed.

connection_timeout.description: Idle connection timeout in seconds before the server closes it.

mtls_enabled.description: Enable mutual TLS: require clients to present a valid certificate signed by a trusted CA.

log_level.description: Logging verbosity level (debug, info, warn, error).

log_file.description: Path to log file (use '-' to log to stdout/stderr).

cipher_suites.description: Ordered list of allowed TLS cipher suites. Leave empty to use defaults.

items.description: A valid TLS cipher suite name (e.g., 'TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384', 'ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256').

trusted_ca_certs.description: List of additional CA certificate paths for mTLS validation (e.g., client CA).

items.description: Absolute path to a trusted CA certificate file (PEM format).

client_hostname_whitelist.description: Whitelist of allowed client certificate Common Names (CN) — used only if mtls_enabled = true.

items.description: Allowed hostname or FQDN matching the client cert CN.

psk_enabled.description: Enable Pre-Shared Key (PSK) mode as an alternative to mTLS.

psk_identity.description: PSK identity string used for client identification (ignored if psk_enabled = false).

psk_secret_path.description: Path to file containing the PSK (raw hex or base64, depending on kxd implementation).

session_timeout.description: TLS session resumption timeout in seconds (0 = disable session caching).

rate_limit_rpm.description: Maximum key exchange requests allowed per minute per client IP address.

experimental_pfs_only.description: Enforce perfect forward secrecy — only allow ECDHE/DHE key exchanges.
